long_biography.plain_text:
Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen used his fortune to create research institutions designed for large, openly shared scientific projects. He and his sister Jody founded the Allen Institute in 2003, commissioning a complete gene-expression atlas of the mouse brain. The organisation later extended that model across cell biology, immunology, neural dynamics and other bioscience fields.

Allen also established Ai2 in Seattle to pursue long-horizon artificial-intelligence research. His fascination with Jimi Hendrix separately inspired the Experience Music Project, which opened as a music museum in 2000. It later broadened into the Museum of Pop Culture, presenting exhibitions and events across music, film, fashion, gaming and other forms of creative expression.
